reply_text:
I found one new dated AI prediction from Hassabis in 2024 and one weaker item that I saw only in someone else's write-up. None of the six claims you have already recorded turned up in pages I could read.

1. **New, August 2024 (Google DeepMind podcast with Hannah Fry, "Unreasonably Effective AI").** He said today's AI systems aren't powerful enough for misuse to be a serious problem, but that "in two three four years time", once systems become agent-like, misuse could cause "serious harm". I read this in a third-party automatic transcript of the YouTube video, so the wording is unpunctuated and should be checked against the recording. The 14 August 2024 date comes from a search-result title; I didn't open that page.

2. **February 2024 (Dwarkesh Patel podcast, published 28 February).** The podcast page cut off before the section on timelines, so I never read his own words. Zvi Mowshowitz's write-up says Hassabis suggested AGI-like systems are on track for 2030 and quotes him as not being surprised "in the next decade." Treat this as secondary only. It reads like the same claims as your "within decade" and "twenty-year plan" files, but those are dated 23 February, which is the Hard Fork episode, so it may be a separate occasion.

The other pages had nothing that qualified:
- **Hard Fork, 23 February:** the transcript page only showed the first few seconds, so I couldn't check your recorded claims.
- **Nobel interview transcript:** has a "next 10 years" line, but it is advice on interdisciplinary science, not a prediction about AI.
- **Axios, October:** no dated predictions.
- **Not reached:** the Nobel lecture and the Google I/O / Gemini 2.0 pages behind your May and December files.

Most search results were 2026 news about his newer "two to three years" AGI estimate, which I've noted under other_years without opening.
